beats.title: Why eigen-things feel confusing; prerequisite mental models
beats.whatChanges: Pi-creature classroom reacts to the title; the det(A-lambda I)=0 equation appears in a speech bubble as a scary artifact; four prerequisite cards (transformations, determinants, linear systems, change of basis) fade in.
beats.invariant: No geometry yet; the equation is planted early so the later derivation lands as the payoff of the whole video.

beats.title: The example transformation [[3,1],[0,2]] and a vector knocked off its span
beats.whatChanges: Grid transforms under the running example matrix; coordinate labels at the tips of i-hat and j-hat morph into the columns of the pinned matrix; a sample vector's span line is drawn, then the transform knocks the vector off it.
beats.invariant: The matrix stays pinned top-left as a foreground mobject over the moving grid; the faded background grid never moves; the span line stays fixed while the vector leaves it.

beats.title: Special vectors that stay on their span: x-axis (x3) and the (-1,1) line (x2)
beats.whatChanges: One vector at a time: (1,-1)-direction vector rides its span; i-hat stretches to 3 with the first matrix column highlighted; a fan of x-axis vectors stretches; the sneaky (-1,1) vector stretches by 2 with its coordinate label moving to the doubled tip; the whole diagonal eigenspace stretches.
beats.invariant: Span lines (maroon) are drawn before each transform and stay put; path_arc=0 makes vectors slide along their spans instead of arcing; the same example matrix stays pinned.

beats.title: Naming: eigenvectors, eigenvalues; negative eigenvalue example
beats.whatChanges: Both eigenline fans shown together; labels 'Stretched by 3/2' morph into 'Eigenvectors ... with eigenvalue 3/2'; a pink non-eigenvector gets knocked off its faded red span for contrast; a separate matrix flips-and-squishes a vector by -1/2 and the span wiggles to emphasize the vector stayed on it.
beats.invariant: The stay-on-span criterion is restated visually for every case; color separates eigen (yellow/maroon gradients) from non-eigen (pink/red).

beats.title: Why care: eigenvector of a 3D rotation is its axis
beats.whatChanges: 3D cube rotates around a fixed vector; the word 'Eigenvector' morphs into 'Axis of rotation'; a friendly 'rotate 30 degrees around [2,3,1]' description morphs into an ugly 3x3 trig matrix; back in 2D the columns-to-basis-vectors reading is shown then criticized as coordinate-bound.
beats.invariant: The message stays: eigen-analysis reveals what a transformation does independent of the coordinate grid.

beats.title: Av = lambda v, rewriting with lambda I, and (A - lambda I)v = 0
beats.whatChanges: The equation Av = lambda v is built term by term with braces naming each part; the RHS becomes (lambda I)v via a lambda-diagonal matrix; terms slide (MoveToTarget with path arcs) into (A - lambda I)v = 0; then a rank-deficient matrix visually squishes the plane to a line while the equation sits in the corner.
beats.invariant: It is the same equation morphing in place, never retyped: v stays yellow and lambda stays maroon through every rearrangement, so each algebra step reads as motion of persistent symbols.

beats.title: Turning the lambda knob until det(A - lambda I) = 0
beats.whatChanges: For A = [[2,2],[1,3]], lambda is animated continuously (0 to 3, back to 0.5, settling at 1); the matrix's diagonal entries, the grid, the unit square, and a live determinant readout all update in lockstep until the plane collapses at lambda = 1; then the found eigenvector rides its span; the four-line reasoning chain Av=lambda v to det=0 is stacked.
beats.invariant: One scalar (lambda) drives numbers and geometry simultaneously, so 'det becomes 0' and 'plane squishes to a line' are visibly the same event. Explicit pause-and-ponder at 9:06.

beats.title: Full computation on the running example: eigenvalues 2 and 3, eigenline of (-1,1)
beats.whatChanges: The lambda symbol physically flies into both diagonal entries making 3-lambda, 2-lambda; entry copies slide out to build the determinant product (3-lambda)(2-lambda)=0; lambda=2 is substituted back into the diagonal, the plane resets and A-2I visibly collapses everything onto the (-1,1) line; then the matrix is restored to unaltered A which stretches that same line by 2.
beats.invariant: Same pinned matrix, same grid, same eigenline as beats 2-4: the algebraic detour ends by replaying the geometric fact it predicts, on the same objects.

beats.title: 90-degree rotation: no eigenvectors, lambda^2 + 1 = 0
beats.whatChanges: The rotation grid turns with a sample vector leaving its span; diagonal entries morph into -lambda; the determinant expands to lambda^2 + 1 with roots i and -i; an on-screen text aside links complex eigenvalues to rotation.
beats.invariant: Same computation choreography as the previous beat, so the failure case (no real roots) is read against the identical procedure.

beats.title: Shear (one eigenline, lambda = 1) and uniform scaling (every vector eigen)
beats.whatChanges: The shear fixes the x-axis fan while everything else slants; the same lambda-into-diagonal and determinant choreography yields (1-lambda)^2 and the single root 1; then 2I scales three random-colored vectors, all eigen with eigenvalue 2.
beats.invariant: Geometry first, algebra second, and they must agree; the x-axis eigen-fan uses the same yellow-to-green gradient as before. Pause-and-ponder at 12:42.

beats.title: Basis vectors as eigenvectors: diagonal matrices and easy powers
beats.whatChanges: A matrix scaling i-hat by -1 and j-hat by 2 is applied one axis at a time; tip coordinates again fly into the matrix columns; diagonal entries pulse in maroon; repeated multiplication collapses to eigenvalue powers, versus an angry pi-creature for the non-diagonal 100th power.
beats.invariant: The tip-coordinates-become-columns move recurs, and lambda-maroon marks diagonal entries as eigenvalues wherever they appear.

beats.title: Change to an eigenbasis; sandwich to a diagonal matrix; closing puzzle
beats.whatChanges: Both eigen-fans reappear on the running example and the transform plays there-and-back; one vector from each fan survives as new basis; their tip coordinates fly in to form the change-of-basis matrix, its inverse copy swings to the left of A; the grid is redrawn skewed to the eigenbasis (with a grey ghost copy) and the transform now reads as pure scaling equal to diag(3,2).
beats.invariant: The same transformation and the same eigenlines from beat 3 persist; only the coordinate grid painted over them changes, which is the whole point of an eigenbasis.
